# Performance ledger (perf-ledger)

> A standing ledger that holds the **filing, adoption decisions, kill criteria and relative priority among candidates** of performance
> candidates. The canonical source for measured values is each snapshot in `docs/research/` — this ledger does not copy numbers
> but points to the source (when it does write a number, it always adds the date). **The canonical source for the phase order and
> status of the whole project is [backlog](backlog.md)** — this ledger only rules within the performance candidates (no double
> ledger).
> Status: ✅ done / 🚧 planned (not yet done) / 🧪 experimental (adoption as the default undecided) /
> ❌ rejected (kept as a record).
> Do not write open TODOs in ✅ / ❌ rows — remaining work is filed in backlog and pointed to.
> Origin of the filing: the D4 leg of the 2026-08-12 exhaustive review (`.claude/reviews/2026-08-12_faef828/findings/D4.md`
> — not tracked by git, so the decision part was moved into this ledger. The old `.claude/reviews/PERFORMANCE.md` is frozen as a
> point-in-time snapshot). The origin of H-5 / H-6 / K-8 / K-9 / L-4 to L-6 is the external review of
> 2026-08-13 (`.claude/reviews/2026-08-13_chatgpt-reviews/` — not tracked by git, so the numbers needed for the decisions were
> copied into this ledger with their dates).

## Policy (the role of the bit-identity check — standing)

> **The role of the bit-identity check (the maintainer's policy 2026-08-13): it is an indicator that the implementation is
> correct, not a goal in itself.** Optimisations that change numbers are allowed as an **opt-in option** — default =
> the reference path (the sha256 checks are frozen there and kept as the indicator); the opt-in side gets an A/B band check against the
> reference path + census; a quality ruling is made only when promoting it to the default (making w8a8 the default is the precedent). **Division of
> quality control (supplement of the same day): the correctness and non-destructiveness of the implementation are verified mechanically with bit identity,
> and the parts where bit identity is not guaranteed are quality-controlled by human review (listening, viewing)** — even when the numbers are much worse,
> the generated result often has not collapsed, so human evaluation takes precedence over numeric indicators (the precedent is "listening
> beats LSD 5.64" when w8a8 became the default). This policy replaces the old "designing a substitute quality check is the precondition". The
> first step of the 2026-08-12 ruling (no preconditions) is done.

2026-09-26: the acceptance contract of the reference path / practical presets is [ADR 0110](decisions/0110-practical-tier-numerics-contract.md)
(contract classes E / C / R / Q, the four-point kernel check, in-device determinism MUST for the practical presets too, sha reference-path rows / practical-preset rows).
Approximate kernels (Q) come in under this contract.

Performance waves ① to ③ of the 2026-08-13 ruling are **done** (wave ① K-4a = ADR 0053 / wave ② the H group = ADR 0054 /
wave ③ K-5 = ADR 0058 and 0060, closed on 2026-08-14 — the history is in each ADR and in research).
From then on, the canonical source for the phase order and open items is [backlog](backlog.md) (this section holds no order).
Ordering constraints among candidates stay in each row's preconditions column (e.g. K-4b after H-4).

In the follow-up investigation of 2026-09-10, residency of Anima's fixed inputs alone could not show an overall gain, and the idea of excluding MTP's first W1 observation
had no stable improvement across 10 conditions either; neither was adopted. Deno's asynchronous map wait was attributed to an internal sleep of the runtime version.
See [the host measurements](research/2026-09-10-codex-mtp-optimization.md#ホスト待ちと既存融合の追加測定) and
[the W1 results](research/2026-09-10-codex-mtp-optimization.md#独立した公式-cpu-検証で停止2209-utc-頃).
This does not mean that latent / scheduler residency or new gate designs were rejected. The remaining work is in backlog.

The evidence is [the measurement record of the QAT review](research/2026-09-19-qat-review.md). The ruling is [ADR 0097 addendum 7](decisions/0097-gemma4-qat-integration.md).

| Status | ID   | Candidate                                                                                          | Preconditions / kill criterion | ------ | ---- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 🧪     | K-45 | A QAT-only integer dot-product linear (SRQ output q × packed integers → i32 accumulation → scale)  | Precondition: using the same compute form as the official mobile makes the result unique regardless of reduction order, which removes the root of the token sequences diverging between CPU and GPU. The accumulation fits in int32 with the current K and value range. It is a new kernel with a different contract from the existing w4a8 ([ADR 0076](decisions/0076-w4a8-linear-execution.md)), and it ripples into the WGSL, estimates, fusion and tests. kill criterion: rejected if the spike measurement gains neither "an improvement in the sequence match rate with the official mobile" nor "speed". It changes the numbers of the default path, so it comes with updates of the bit-identity checks and the goldens. **2026-09-19 refutation** ([decode speed investigation](research/2026-09-19-qat-speed-recon.md) §9 cluster C): the expected gain is 0.9 ms/token of GPU (about half of the estimate at filing, including the GEMV efficiency ideas H1 / H2). The kill decision of step 0 comes first (no new kernel needed — a standalone A/B of a comparison shader that replaces only the multiply-add expansion with the minimal instruction form; rejected if under 25% on i2 262144×1536). The implementation point is inside the linear→SRQ fusion kernel (Route A: unpack the weight word → −z → pack4xI8 → dot4I8Packed, no row sums needed / Route B: unsigned dot product + activation bias a^0x80 + 2 correction terms in the epilogue). dot4U8Packed / dot4I8Packed have the same signedness on both sides, so the mixed form "unsigned weights × signed activations" cannot be written as is. **Step 0 passed (2026-09-19, research §14)**: on the occupancy-saturated lm_head shape the minimal instruction form is 2.1 times, on the gate/up shape 2.7 times, past the check. But the bottleneck is not the ALU but **the number of activation loads** (down shape 83% / i4 g512 48% / gate and up 41%, arithmetic 0.3% / 8% / 23%, only lm_head 36%), and the arithmetic of `dot4I8Packed` itself is free. The shape of step 1 needs a decision: packed int8 activations + the current f32 FMA (portable) first, and the integer dot product only for the lm_head shape. **Step 1a implemented** (`57416eb` + follow-up, ADR 0105, option `packedStaticQuantize` default false, u32 match on every shape, id sequences match). A/B (research §16): packing only the 4 shapes that measured effective (K length × lanes 32) gives **Chrome +8.3% / GPU −0.57 ms/token, Deno +1.5 to 2.9%** (packing every shape cancels out through insufficient occupancy of the SRQ kernel and worse lanes 2/4 shapes). **2026-09-20**: declared in `i4-fast` (ADR 0105 addendum 2, an option in hub's SessionSpec + distribution rebuild). M2 follow-up = speed-neutral (35.8 / 35.9 tok/s); at first the id sequences of the English prompt diverged between off/on → the cause was how Metal contracts fma, and fixing the parallel GEMV family to explicit fma made the id sequences match (ADR 0105 addendum 4, research §16.1). **Step 1b is rejected**: the real model's lm_head has no int8 activations (the SRQ scale of the official checkpoint is 0 = identity, so the recipe does not insert it), the upper bound is 36% arithmetic of lm_head's 0.24 ms/token ≈ 0.09 ms (1.3% of the GPU), and going integer would need dynamic quantisation that the official one does not have either (the same decision as K-52) |
| 🚧     | K-46 | int8 KV cache for QAT (official `k_cache_scale` / `v_cache_scale`, staged plan = full layers only) | Precondition: the official checkpoint has a fixed scale per layer. The full layers alone take most of the gain (E2B 32k 384 → 96 MiB). The sliding layers are a fixed buffer of window 512 and can stay out of scope. Comes with extending the dtype of the states form (generation-context / state-attention / estimates / the states conversion of exporter). kill criterion: not started while the product's target context length stays at a few thousand. int8 KV changes the numbers, so it is rejected if quality drops. **2026-09-19 refutation** ([decode speed investigation](research/2026-09-19-qat-speed-recon.md) §7.2 / cluster K): it does not help decode speed (at L≈100 the KV path is 0.15 ms/token, and even at 16k context attention is latency-bound, so the "bandwidth-bound" start condition does not hold) — **taken out of the speed phase and treated as an item about memory and the capacity ceiling** (KV 60 → 15 MiB at capacity 4096, 1,548 → 387 MiB at 131k, the binding limit of the full slots relaxes 4 times). sliding reads 24,576 B per position, twice the full layers, so the staged plan of "full only" is dropped and both are done at once. There is no scale collision on shared slots (the `k/v_cache_scale` of shared layers match the source; `v_cache_scale` is suspected not to be calibrated per layer). Start after a quality acceptance for contexts beyond 512 is in place                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| 🚧     | K-47 | Scale duplication caused by `group_size` being required for `i4` (E2B 2.4 MB / E4B 16.7 MiB)       | Precondition: QAT's fixed I4 fills in by duplicating the upstream per-row scale for the number of groups. The value is fully constant within a row, so the numbers do not change, but the distribution bytes and residency grow purely, and GEMV / GEMM fetch the scale again for every word. Resolving it needs a format change that allows a per-row scale (without `group_size`) for `i4` as for `i2`. kill criterion: rejected if a reduction of about 0.78% of the 2.25 GB E4B distribution is not worth the ripple into IR, exporter, every i4 kernel, the WGSL snapshots and the published assets. That hoisting may break bit identity is the same point as i8 in [ADR 0019](decisions/0019-i8-weight-execution.md). **2026-09-19 refutation** ([decode speed investigation](research/2026-09-19-qat-speed-recon.md) cluster H2): rejected as a speed idea — an i4 word = 32 elements, so scale reads are only 48 per column, and K-45 takes the effect of folding ZP and scale into the epilogue without a format change. Kept only as a distribution-size item ## 2026-09-19 attribution of decode speed and what to try next

The evidence is the [decode speed investigation](research/2026-09-19-qat-speed-recon.md) (cost model, refutations and order in §9 to 10). The current state on Chrome is a wall of 10.03 ms / GPU 6.79 ms after ADR 0103 (2026-09-25 note: after the packed activations of ADR 0105 the GPU is 6.63 ms — in a different measurement round with a baseline of 7.20 ms, [research §16](research/2026-09-19-qat-speed-recon.md)). Gains are marginal values when combined (ms/token).

The existing rewind rejects every context with sliding slots (ADR 0066 addendum 2), so it cannot be used for Gemma, which has sliding layers. Depth 2 or more needs a revision of the current contract "while a run awaits commit, the next run is rejected", and whether to allow several runs awaiting commit or to limit acceptance to models without sliding is decided in ADR 0066 before starting) + a greedy-only option (temperature > 0 uses the host RNG) + the diagnostic path stays without run-ahead (ADR 0054 decision 2). Expected: Deno −5 ms (when combined with H-26, −8 alone) / Chrome up to −2.2 ms. kill criterion: in an ABBA of depth 1/2/4/8, unless Chrome's wall−GPU difference of 3.3 to 4.1 (measured 2026-09-19, research §13) → drops below 1 ms, it is judged Deno-only and rejected (H-29 is revived)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

Raising the manifest's requiredLimits (256 MiB → a single binding of 1.13 GiB), giving up the shard lazy loading of ADR 0085 decision 3, a staged option that makes it resident only on machines that can take the full budget (whether M2's VRAM allows it is the maintainer's real machine). Check: bit match of `ple.probe` + exact match of the id sequences of 64 / 256 tokens (speed is not looked at). Standalone gain 0.25 ms. **2026-09-20**: remaining item ① (+1 fence for decode with temperature > 0 / with diagnostics) is resolved by `Session.enqueueRead` (ADR 0054 addendum) — neutral with host on Deno's default sampler (research §15.1). Remaining item ② is attributed (research §15.2): not the language or the gather, but a phenomenon where on Chrome a large VRAM occupancy makes the host side of the prefill run grow by +120 ms up to a plateau from the 8th generation on (reproduces on host too when the budget is raised; does not occur on Deno). The countermeasure is pooling the temporary buffers of prefill, handled in the step of H-27 / making residency the default. **2026-09-25 note (bringing the preconditions up to date)**: the implementation does not change the manifest's requiredLimits — `acquireGpu` requests the adapter's measured values, and at load time compares them with `maxStorageBufferBindingSize` / `maxBufferSize` and fails loudly if short (the 2026-09-19 addendum "resident amount and binding limits" of [ADR 0085](decisions/0085-ple-host-gather.md)). Shard lazy loading is retired too, and the current loading mechanism is the 2026-09-24 addendum (container path) of the same ADR. **2026-09-25 correction (countermeasure for remaining item ②)**: "the countermeasure is pooling the temporary buffers of prefill" above is withdrawn — the prefill of a hit run keeps its intermediates resident in the slot backing, and the only per-run arena allocation is the readback staging (the 2026-09-25 addendum of research §15.2). What is allocated and destroyed per generation is the per-sequence GenerationContext (KV ≈50 MB) and the re-baking of its state bind group; the attribution awaits re-measurement (recording `allocCount` / `rebindCount` + an arm that reuses the context) |

On local, every Session build digests every block (on every generation for anima / irodori / sbv2, which build a Session per generation; at 938 MiB/s, 1 GiB of weights ≈1.1 s — speculation). For gemma4 E2B on local, digest 4.1 → 1.1 s (extrapolated from 3,702 MiB/s); the dominant term is `shardWaitMs` 2.1 s (75% of the PLE build — the name and value of that time; renamed to `supplyWaitMs` in 0.13.0). Precondition: unify in an ADR the mismatch of the trust policy where hub's local source trusts sha256 while runtime treats the same local as unverified and digests it every time (how to handle TOCTOU — the same ruling as backlog later's "with an unverified source (local), row reads of host PLE…"). Measure first: compare `buildStats.supplyWaitMs` before and after on local / warm. kill: gemma4 local fromPretrained under −15%                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

If the rows of the same block are fewer than 32, all of them become row reads, and the same block is read and digested as many times as there are rows (a 9.4 GiB digest for 300 rows — speculation), with 16 × 32 MiB = 512 MiB at the same time (outside the budget). Precondition: L-16's remembering of verified blocks (the same root). In addition, throttle the concurrent issue of row reads by bytes rather than count (the same approach as hub's `createByteAdmission`). kill (a line set at filing — not in FB3): after L-16 the wall of the prefill gather shrinks by less than 5%                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| 🚧     | L-18 | The scan-type hold window keeps the last part for the whole lifetime of a component (a memory item)                                                        | Findings E-PF3-1 / W-DS2-4 (same root). Deno + HF only, upper bound "number of components × length of the last part". The root is L-14 option a (the scan type disappears from the first-party paths). Stopgap: add an optional `release?()` to `BlockSource` and call it after the last batch (a change of the public surface; unless done together with L-14 option b, the window empties on every PLE row read). kill: this row closes if L-14 option a goes in                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| 🚧     | L-19 | The exporter pulls the weights of piece-split tensors twice (position of the scale)                                                                        | Finding W-EX1-5. It flows in the order `[piece0, scale]` → piece1, so for each quantized tensor over 32 MiB packed, one extra storage conversion runs (twice in split form, 4 times in single form). Only the CPU time of export; unrelated to the distribution and runtime. Option a: swap to `head = [scale, piece0]` (the placement changes and every sha256 of the distribution moves, so it rides along the next re-export phase) / option b: keep the result of the storage conversion in a second entry for the scale (placement unchanged). kill (a line set at filing — not in FB3): the wall of an export containing such tensors shrinks by less than 5%                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

An OOM of `createBuffer` is non-fatal, but an OOM of the staging of `queue.writeBuffer` makes wgpu lose the device on the spot, Deno delivers it as an ordinary `GPUOutOfMemoryError`, and `device.lost` does not resolve until the next call that goes through validation. The reproduction on B570 (`evict-probe.ts --dummy-gib 6`) succeeds on the second image, the PNG sha matches the first, the 4 residency e2e rows are green. ## 2026-10-10 seams in Wan's DiT passes (from the maintainer's observation)

The evidence is the maintainer's observation of 2026-10-10 (the GPU graph of the task manager while running Wan2.2's I2V in Chrome on an RTX 5070 Ti — between the DiT steps and
in the VAE stage, seams where utilisation drops to 0 appear periodically. With more frames each step takes longer and the seams become relatively less frequent). gpu-lab's
JSON (`outputs/bench-browser/wan-browser-2026-10-10T14-11-07.191Z.json`, not tracked by git) holds only the stage durations and cannot separate the seams. On the development machine
(Deno, RTX 3080 Ti, about 12 s per pass) the seams are 0.5 s or less, and the utilisation trough was 84%. The shape of the DiT loop is
`runWanDenoise` in `packages/models/src/wan/dit-loop.ts` (1 step = 2 serial passes uncond → cond; per pass it uploads the context
([1, 512, 4096] f32, 8 MiB), RoPE and tokens to `session.run`, reads the output back and does unpatchify → CFG → UniPC → patchify on the host).

| Status | ID   | Candidate                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Preconditions / kill criterion                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------ | ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| ❌     | H-37 | Seams in Wan's DiT passes (re-uploads, readbacks, CFG / UniPC on the host). Candidates ① queue uncond / cond back to back and read back once ② keep the context and RoPE, which do not change between steps, resident ③ move CFG / UniPC to the GPU (the same form as anima's H-33). For the VAE stage the tile stitching was measured (the per-tile readback is included in the tile's interval and not separated — the estimate from byte counts is in research) | **Rejected (measured 2026-10-15 — [research](research/2026-10-15-wan-dit-seams-h37.md))**: with the practical preset, T2V, 1280×704 at 33 / 121 frames, the estimated total of the seams (per-pass uploads, readbacks, host patchify / unpatchify / CFG / UniPC / finiteness checks) is 0.34 to 1.30% of a step (after the in-generation correction; Deno on RTX 3080 Ti and Chrome on RTX 5070 Ti, once each; Chrome's 121 frames is 0.72% by conversion), far below the kill line of 5%. Almost all of a step is the time of the 2 runs (forwards). The VAE stitching is also 0.76 to 1.14% of the VAE stage. Even with all 3 candidates, at most about 1.3% of a step can be taken (estimate), and ③ comes with rebuilding the sha rows. Condition to resume = when the forward gets much faster and the share of the seams approaches 5% (measurable with the same tools) |

## 2026-10-11 attention row-block budget (capacity — ADR 0124)

The evidence is the maintainer's ruling 6 = a (2026-10-11) and ADR [0124](decisions/0124-attention-row-block-budget.md). On the development machine (RTX 3080 Ti, 12,288 MiB),
Wan2.2's 1280×704×121 (practical preset) has a VRAM peak of 11,361 MiB in the DiT stage and about 0.9 GiB of headroom (ADR 0121 — measured). Splitting the row blocks
more finely than the binding limit shrinks the momentary temporaries of attention. It is bit-identical, so it is not a numerics option but a resource policy (the maintainer chooses the trade between speed and capacity).

| Status | ID   | Candidate                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Preconditions / kill criterion                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------ | ---- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| ✅     | L-25 | Lower the momentary VRAM peak of attention with `SessionOptions.attentionRowBlockMaxBytes` (the cap per row-block temporary = min(binding limit, budget), output bit-identical). The runtime knob and the estimate are in (ADR 0124). Adopted as a runtime opt-in; no Wan default and no models hook | Step 4b measurement (2026-10-11, RTX 3080 Ti, Deno, the practical preset of the Wan2.2 DiT at 121 frames — [research 2026-10-11](research/2026-10-11-row-block-budget-stage-4b.md), the opt-in `KARUME_WAN_TI2V_ROW_BLOCK_PROBE=1` of `packages/models/tests/e2e_wan_ti2v_dit_test.ts`): with no budget / 1 GiB / 512 MiB / 256 MiB, backing 5.97 / 4.99 / 4.51 / 4.33 GiB, VRAM peak of the whole GPU 11,308 / 10,304 / 9,811 / 9,622 MiB (monotonically down). The total GPU time of the measurement mode is 37.3 / 35.8 / 36.3 / 46.6 s (1 GiB and 512 MiB within the noise; 256 MiB is +24.9%, almost all of the increase in `attention_pv`). The wall clock swung with thermal throttling and is not used as speed material. The output is bit-identical with no budget in the layer-1 u32 A/B (17 / 121 frames, 2 presets). The per-stage GPU time is material for the preconditions of the fast path of online softmax (outside the boundary of ADR 0124 decision 9), in the same research. Chrome's point is not measured. **Ruling 39 = a (the maintainer 2026-10-11)**: not put into Wan's default, and no hook is added to models (`WanTi2vPipeline`) or gpu-lab either (121 frames fit in the 12 GiB class without a budget, so there is no problem to solve; the cost in wall clock could not be ruled out — the section on the results of step 4b of ADR 0124). Add a hook if a problem appears |

## 2026-10-23 FlashAttention-2 recon for the Wan DiT (subgroups / workgroup storage)

The evidence is the [recon](research/2026-10-23-flash-attention-webgpu-recon.md) (web sweep + probes + two measurements on the RTX 3080 Ti, Node + Dawn): one DiT forward at S = 27,280 (practical preset)
is 24.2 s of GPU time, the three attention kernels 64% of it and ② row statistics 16.4%; ①QK runs at 32 TOPS and ③PV at 19 TOPS against a measured dp4a ceiling of 65 TOPS, so both are compute-bound and the S round trip
mostly hides behind arithmetic. Subgroup matrix (the matrix units) is exposed only behind Dawn's `allow_unsafe_apis` / Chrome's `--enable-unsafe-webgpu` and the proposal is Draft.

| Status | ID   | Candidate                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Preconditions / kill criterion                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------ | ---- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| ✅     | K-82 | Online (FlashAttention-2-style) attention for the Wan DiT as an a8 opt-in: one kernel per query row block that streams int8 K / V tiles sized by the granted `maxComputeWorkgroupStorageSize` (Bc = 128 / 64 / 32 at 48 / 32 / 16 KiB), keeps the running max / sum and an f32 O, builds P̃ per key tile as today's ③PV does, and folds the integer block result into O with the rescale (SageBwd's form) — removes ② and the S round trip | Filed 2026-10-23 (the maintainer: measure first, then decide on a spike). Upper bound from the measurement: ×1.34 on the attention kernels (the ② share), 16% of the forward, before the online kernel's own costs. Kill: a standalone spike at S = 8k / 27k, D = 128, below ×1.3 on the attention kernels against the current three dispatches (the K-5b line). **Spike 2026-10-23 (recon §10.2)**: ×1.46 at S = 27,280 and ×1.04–1.15 at S = 7,920 against the current three dispatches (self-attention keys), subgroup shuffle reduce, bank-conflict-free tile layouts; ×1.61 / ×1.28 with the interleaved `Vᵀ` key order done on the host — passes the line at the long shape, not at the short one. **Done 2026-10-23 (ADR 0132)**: `attentionScoreStorage: "none"`, the Wan2.2 default preset `f16+dit8-a8-attn8-online`; in the DiT measured mode at S = 27,280 attention 18.4 → 12.5 s (×1.47 cold; ×1.25 against the morning's baseline), forward 29.3 → 21.7 s; A/B 33f relRMS 4.23e-2 (ADR 0132 Results). Headroom left: the host-side Vᵀ key order (+10% in the spike), Bc = 128 on 48 KiB devices. The subgroup-matrix path (①③'s arithmetic, 16 of the 24 s): the spike (recon §10.1) reads the runtime's packed i8 exactly and reaches 91 TOPS on a naive GEMM; still only behind `allow_unsafe_apis` — a candidate only as a Node-only opt-in, not filed |
